claims.claim: the real top-1,000,000 internet sites are bulk-loaded into the net (2.05 GB of weights) - a genuine copy of a slice of the live internet on this machine
nearest-centroid routing works on real internet geometry: querying a famous site returns its real web neighbors (char-ngram home space, cosine)
a 20% random outage (200,000 sites killed) leaves 800,000 survivors still routed - functionality preserved with no repair unit
local flow on a real 1000-site slice at dim=128 costs 862 ms/step and the local heal recovers spacing (1.003 -> 1.052)

verdict: SUPPORTED (measured): the top-1M real sites are loaded, routed through the 20% outage, and a real slice flows with self-healing spacing recovery - 'copy the internet' at the scale this machine can honestly hold (full internet ~10^13 URLs needs a cluster)
